newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends firmer on c.bank intervention.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends firmer on c.bank intervention.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Friday stronger at 6,800/7,200 to the dollar against 7,000/500 in early trading as a midday with help from a midday central bank (BNR) intervention, traders said.
"Inflows on the money market helped the dollar in early trading when it climbed to 7,500/8,000, but the central bank stepped in immediately to mop up leu funds," said one trader.
"It was a clear attempt to support the leu," said another, estimating that the BNR sold some $7.0 million and bought around $2.0 million.
BNR officials confirmed the central bank's actions on Friday but declined to confirm the size of the intervention, which it called "a test."
"I wouldn't call it an intervention, it was rather a test," said BNR spokesman Adrian Vasilescu, without elaborating.
Some dealers speculated that the BNR was poised to lash out at banks that had not extended their rollover T-bills on offer on Friday. Results of Friday's subscription were not available.

Short-term money market rates fell to some 215/230 percent from near 300 percent in the early hours as the market digested Thursday's drop to 226.31 percent from 426.5 percent in the average auctioned credit rate.
On Friday, the BNR also postponed for the second week in a row announcing a new method of computing the reference exchange rate for the leu currency but gave no reason for the delay.
Traders said the delay might affect the banks, because minimum reserves on banks' hard currency deposits, held in leu currency with the central bank, are converted at that rate.
"This will trigger an artificial rise in reserve targets as the 7,744 level of the reference rate is by far weaker than the market rates," said one dealer with a state bank.
Last month, the BNR gave up computing the leu's reference rate after restoring local dealer licences to 24 banks, which are now market makers along with four others.
The reference rate is frozen at 7,744 lei to the dollar, computed on February 19. Vasilescu said that level would remain effective until a new method was announced.
Banks' quotes continued to reflect a wide range, with leu-dollar rates from 6,000/100 to 7,400/8,400.
Leu-dollar retail rates were flat near 6,200/700 to 6,800/7,150.
